relations.note: AWS is Anthropic's primary cloud; trains on Trainium

deals.summary: Anthropic committed to spend at least $110.0B with Amazon between May 2026 and April 2036 regardless of usage, with a true-up if actual spend falls short (S-1).

evidence.quote: In April 2026, we entered into an agreement with Amazon, pursuant to which we committed to spend an aggregate of at least $110.0 billion between May 2026 and April 2036, regardless of actual usage.

relations.note: Anthropic also uses Google Cloud TPUs at large scale

deals.summary: At least about $114.5B with Google, April 2026 to July 2033, regardless of usage, with a true-up if spend falls short. Agreed March 2026, amended May to August 2026.

evidence.quote: In March 2026, we entered into an agreement with Google, which was subsequently amended between May and August 2026, and pursuant to which we committed to spend at least approximately $114.5 billion between April 2026 and July 2033, regardless of actual usage.

relations.note: Additional TPU compute 2028 to 2031 from TPU providers including Google; Anthropic estimates $125.0B to $150.0B (S-1)

deals.summary: Additional TPU compute from TPU providers including Google, delivered 2028 to 2031. Anthropic estimates the payments at about $125.0B to $150.0B, outside the commitments table.

evidence.quote: In addition, we also committed to procure additional TPU compute from TPU providers, including Google, to be delivered between 2028 and 2031.
We estimate the aggregate future payments for such additional compute to be approximately $125.0 billion to $150.0 billion, which are not included in the contractual commitments table above.

relations.note: Committed to spend at least $44.9B with Microsoft, November 2026 to May 2033 (S-1)

deals.summary: At least $44.9B with Microsoft, November 2026 to May 2033, regardless of usage. Agreed November 2025, amended February and October 2026.

evidence.quote: In November 2025, we entered into an agreement with Microsoft, which was subsequently amended in February and October 2026, pursuant to which we committed to spend an aggregate of at least $44.9 billion between November 2026 and May 2033, regardless of actual usage.

relations.note: Up to $120.5B for Nvidia GPU compute from SpaceXAI (formerly X.AI LLC), terms into 2029 (S-1)

deals.summary: Up to $120.5B for compute powered by Nvidia GPUs from SpaceX.AI LLC (formerly X.AI LLC, a SpaceX subsidiary), about $3.1B a month once all capacity is delivered (expected December 2026). Cancellable on 90 days' notice after the initial periods end in January and March 2027.

evidence.quote: Between May and October 2026, we entered into and amended several agreements with SpaceX.AI LLC (formerly known as X.AI LLC) (“SpaceXAI”), a wholly owned subsidiary of Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (collectively, the “SpaceXAI Arrangements”), to access compute powered by NVIDIA GPUs.

Under the SpaceXAI Arrangements, we agreed to spend an aggregate of up to $120.5 billion over terms extending into 2029, consisting of approximately $3.1 billion in the aggregate per month once all capacity has been delivered, which we expect in December 2026, with different fees during capacity ramping periods.

relations.note: Up to about $44.6B for Nvidia GPU compute from Nscale, terms into 2033 (S-1)

deals.summary: Up to about $44.6B for Nvidia GPU compute from Nscale, terms into 2033, fees only as capacity is delivered and accepted. Nscale must use best efforts to finance the GPUs and data centers.

evidence.quote: Under the Nscale Services Agreements, we agreed to spend an aggregate of up to approximately $44.6 billion over terms extending into 2033, with fees accruing only as capacity is delivered to and accepted by us.

relations.note: About $41.3B for Nvidia GPU compute from Lambda, terms into 2034 (S-1)

deals.summary: About $41.3B for Nvidia GPU compute from Lambda, terms into 2034. The August 2026 agreement (about $34.9B of it) can be ended if Lambda does not secure the facility lease in time.

evidence.quote: Under the Lambda Agreements, we agreed to spend an aggregate of approximately $41.3 billion over terms extending into 2034, with fees accruing only as capacity is delivered to and accepted by us.
Under our August 2026 agreement, which represents approximately $34.9 billion of the aggregate commitment, either party may terminate if Lambda does not timely secure the facility lease.

relations.note: Five-year master equipment leases for TPU-based compute; rent about $161.2B excluding interest (S-1)

deals.summary: Five-year master equipment leases with Broadcom giving Anthropic TPU-based compute in data centers others operate. Rent about $161.2B excluding interest; part came online in 2026, more from 2027.

evidence.quote: Our rent payments over the life of these leases are equal to an aggregate of approximately $161.2 billion excluding interest, with rent payable in quarterly installments and payment obligations typically commencing upon AI infrastructure equipment becoming “ready for service” at the applicable data center facility.
The Lease Arrangements provide us with access to TPU-based compute capacity, a portion of which began to come online in 2026, with additional capacity expected to come online starting in 2027.

deals.summary: Anthropic may issue up to $42.0B of convertible notes to Broadcom or a designated financial partner, if needed, to finance the 2026 lease.

evidence.quote: In addition, we have the ability to issue, if needed, up to $42.0 billion in aggregate principal amount of convertible promissory notes to Broadcom or, subject to our consent (not to be unreasonably withheld), a designated financial partner pursuant to a note purchase agreement that we entered into with Broadcom in March 2026 (the “Infrastructure Partner 2026 NPA”) to finance obligations under the 2026 Lease Arrangement.

relations.note: Hardware Supply Agreement: AMD Helios rack-scale systems from 2027; expected spend above $20.0B for the initial capacity (S-1)

deals.summary: Initial tranche of compute in 2027 on AMD Helios rack-scale systems. No fixed dollar amount; Anthropic expects more than $20.0B if it takes the full initial capacity, with an option on about as much again.

evidence.quote: Under the Hardware Supply Agreement with AMD, we committed to obtain an initial tranche of compute capacity in calendar year 2027 by purchasing AMD-based Helios rack-scale systems from approved manufacturers or by accessing such systems through third-party service providers, provided certain conditions related to deployment proposals are met.

If we procure the full amount of this initial committed capacity, we expect aggregate expenditures to exceed $20.0 billion over the term of the agreement, which are not included in the contractual commitments table above.

deals.summary: About $6.2B of Amazon convertible notes outstanding at 30 June 2026 (2023 agreement $2,186M, 2024 agreement $4,017M). Conversion is capped at 12% of Anthropic's capitalization unless Amazon waives it. An April 2026 agreement adds potential future financing capacity.

evidence.quote: Our NPAs with Amazon consist of the Amazon 2023 NPA and the Amazon 2024 NPA, pursuant to which we previously issued convertible promissory notes, approximately $6.2 billion aggregate principal amount of which remains outstanding

unless Amazon elects in its sole discretion to waive the limitation, no portion of a note converts to the extent that, immediately following the conversion, Amazon would hold more than 12% of our capitalization

predictions.statement: Cloud marketplaces will account for more than half of Anthropic's revenue for full-year 2026.
predictions.basis: The marketplace share rose from about 11% (2023) to 32% (2024), 47% (2025) and 48% (first half of 2026), per the S-1.

predictions.statement: Anthropic will report a positive Adjusted Operating Margin for full-year 2026.
predictions.basis: Adjusted Operating Margin moved from minus 159% in the first half of 2025 to plus 10% in the first half of 2026, and to 19% in the second quarter of 2026, per the S-1.

implications.headline: Distribution beat advertising
implications.body: In the first half of 2026, fees to channel partners rose by $2.7B against $273M more for marketing and advertising, and about 48% of revenue came through cloud marketplaces. For an AI product, the marketplace listing and the integrator network are primary channels.

implications.headline: Cheaper intelligence grew usage
implications.body: Opus 4.5 launched with a lower price per task than Opus 4.1, and quarter-over-quarter revenue growth went from 48% to 132%. Build so you can switch models as price per task falls.

implications.headline: Compute is the constraint, contracted for a decade
implications.body: The S-1 lists compute arrangements with Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Broadcom, SpaceXAI, Nscale, Lambda and AMD, with terms running to 2036. Whoever supplies compute shapes which models get built and what they cost.

entity_update.tagline: Maker of Claude; filed to list on Nasdaq as ANT on 26 Oct 2026
entity_update.story: Anthropic builds the Claude family of models and sells them through its own apps, its API and all three major clouds. It filed its Form S-1 on 26 October 2026 to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market as ANT. Revenue was $4.6 billion in 2025 and $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026. Claude is trained and served on four chip families (AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs and AMD GPUs), and the S-1 lists compute arrangements with Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Broadcom, SpaceXAI, Nscale, Lambda and AMD on terms running to 2036.
